facts.text: Brookfield was originally called Grossdale, founded in 1889 by Samuel Eberly Gross who sold lots along the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy Railroad.
The village’s oldest building, the Grossdale Train Station built in the 1880s, now houses the Brookfield Historical Society and is on the National Register.
In 1981 the original train station was moved a few hundred feet east across the tracks to its current location, preserving its historic charm.
Brookfield earned a replica of the Liberty Bell during its Bicentennial celebrations, one of only 111 copies cast from the same mold as the original.
The village hosts the Galloping Ghost Arcade, the largest video arcade in the U.S., boasting over 1,050 games and pinball machines.
North Kiwanis Park is the site of annual events like German Fest, Fall Fest, Battle of the Bands, and the Brookfield Fourth of July Parade.
